context.body: Divine constancy supports both severe purification and Jacob’s preservation.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The LORD announces a messenger and sudden coming, compares the arrival to refining fire, purifies worship, judges oppression, and grounds survival in divine constancy.
observations.label: The unchanging God comes to refine and judge: action

observations.body: Priests and people face purification; vulnerable people’s treatment becomes evidence in judgment.
observations.label: The unchanging God comes to refine and judge: response

observations.body: messenger · who can endure? · refiner’s fire · I do not change
observations.label: Words in Malachi 3:1–6

payload.posture: Read Malachi 3:1–6 as future and faithfulness evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: “I do not change” appears inside covenant judgment and mercy, not as an abstract denial of every responsive action.
payload.title: The unchanging God comes to refine and judge
